text:
Search found related streaming extrema literature, but no direct match for this exact labeled, distance-constrained pair query. Lemire’s [streaming maximum–minimum filter](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0610046) concerns sliding-window extrema; it does not establish the requested algorithm. The following exact solution follows directly from the objective: for fixed right endpoint l, max over eligible k of min(a[k], a[l]) equals min(a[l], max eligible a[k]), where eligibility requires k ≤ l−d and label[k] ≠ label[l].

Maintain the two largest prefix maxima belonging to distinct labels, retaining a witness index for each. Before querying l, insert index l−d: update its entry if its label is already represented; otherwise compare it with the two retained entries, then reorder. Use the largest entry unless its label equals label[l], in which case use the second; combine with a[l] using min and update the global best. Missing eligible entries contribute −∞, so negative scores remain correct. For d ≥ 1, this computes the exact answer in O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary state with random-access input; a strict stream needs an O(d) delay buffer. If a causal application has n separate score rows, each of length O(n), applying this scan independently gives O(n²) total computation, avoiding cubic pair enumeration. Blocking alone reduces peak memory without changing enumeration complexity.
